agentCan: Author the entire app project and app-hsmeta.json (auth type, distribution, redirect URLs, scope buckets)
Implement the OAuth server (authorize URL, code exchange, refresh) and granted-scope handling
Draft the listing packet (shared-data table mapped to scopes, support and policy pages)

approval.trigger: No HubSpot review to distribute: sign the Acceptable Use Policy and any account can install via your install URL. BUT unlisted apps are capped at 25 installs. Removing the cap requires Marketplace listing, which is manually reviewed by the HubSpot Ecosystem Quality team and itself requires at least 3 active, unique, unaffiliated production installs with real app activity in the past 30 days.
approval.wait: Listing: initial review within 10 business days; the full review-and-feedback process should take no more than 60 days from first feedback (both stated by HubSpot)

blockers.detail: Until your app is reviewed and listed, installs stop at 25 customer accounts (developer test accounts excluded). Hitting the cap mid-onboarding is a documented partner pain point, and you cannot even apply to lift it until you have 3 real external installs, so recruit those early and deliberately inside your allowance.
blockers.howToClear: Sign the AUP, recruit 3 unaffiliated production installs fast, and start the listing process long before you approach 25.
blockers.title: The 25-install cap is the real gate

blockers.detail: Until the AUP is signed from the app's Distribution tab, the app can only be installed into developer test accounts. It is one click and a signature, but it is a hard gate that is easy to miss because the app works fine in testing.
blockers.howToClear: Sign it on day one, even if you never intend to create a listing (you can close the publishing panel right after).
blockers.title: Unsigned AUP = test accounts only

blockers.detail: No verified domain: install page warns the app 'hasn't been verified'. Verified domain but unlisted: banner says not reviewed/approved. Fully unreviewed: the installer must click through a dialog and type 'I accept the risk'. Only a listed app installs with no warning.
blockers.howToClear: Verify your domain (TXT record; usually within an hour, up to 48 hrs DNS propagation) at minimum, and list when the warnings start costing conversions.
blockers.title: Layered install-time trust warnings

alternatives: Privately distributed OAuth app (distribution: private): same OAuth, but installs only into allowlisted accounts, capped at 10
Legacy 'private app': a static token for ONE account created by its super admin; no install flow, not for multi-customer products (the naming trap to avoid)
flavor.recommended: Public app in a developer project: distribution 'marketplace' + auth.type 'oauth' in app-hsmeta.json
flavor.why: This is the only flavor third parties install into their own HubSpot accounts via an install URL, and the only uncapped path (after listing). 'Connected apps' is just HubSpot's customer-facing name for the installed state. Choose marketplace distribution even if you never list: listing and distribution are decoupled.

humanMust: Create the HubSpot account and upload the app project under it
Retrieve and protect the client secret
Sign the Acceptable Use Policy (a person must accept it)
Add the DNS TXT record for domain verification
Recruit the first 3 unaffiliated production installs and run the listing process
name: HubSpot
nuances: Scopes live in three buckets in app-hsmeta.json: requiredScopes (install fails without all), optionalScopes (dropped silently if the account lacks the tool/tier), conditionallyRequiredScopes (required only when included in the install URL). Tier-dependent scopes belong in optional/conditional, and your token handling must check which optional scopes were actually granted.
Listing requirement with teeth: your app must USE all of the scopes it requests; unused scopes must be removed, and the listing's Shared data table must match the scopes exactly.

Installers must be super admins, or hold HubSpot Marketplace access permission plus permissions matching every scope group you request (e.g. requesting crm.import means the installer needs the Import permission).

Scope additions after listing appear not to require re-review (staff statement, flagged in evidence), but existing installs likely need to reinstall for new-scope functionality, and your listing must be updated to stay compliant.
Up to 10 free developer test accounts with 90-day enterprise trials are available for development.
prerequisites: A HubSpot account with Development access (no paid subscription needed to build)
The HubSpot CLI for scaffolding/uploading the app project
At least one HTTPS redirect URL (http://localhost allowed only for testing)
A domain you control (for the verification TXT record)

steps.detail: In app-hsmeta.json declare: name, description, logo, supportEmail, documentationUrl, supportUrl; auth.type = 'oauth'; distribution = 'marketplace'; redirectUrls (HTTPS required). Scopes go in three buckets: requiredScopes (at least one; granular per-object, e.g. crm.objects.contacts.read), optionalScopes, conditionallyRequiredScopes. Client ID and secret appear on the app's Auth tab in the portal.
steps.title: Create the app project and configure auth

steps.detail: Build the authorize URL (app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, scope, redirect_uri), handle the code redirect, exchange code + client secret for access/refresh tokens, refresh on expiry. Required scopes in your config MUST be in the URL's scope parameter or the auth page errors; accounts lacking a required scope's tool also error, which is what optional scopes are for.
steps.title: Implement the OAuth server flow

steps.detail: Distribution tab > Begin publishing > sign the AUP. Until you do, installs are limited to developer test accounts. You can close the panel immediately after signing and never create a listing.
steps.title: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy

steps.detail: Development > Domain > Verify a domain: add the TXT record HubSpot provides. Stated: usually completes within an hour, up to 48 hours for DNS propagation. One verified domain per developer account covers all its apps; removing the TXT record brings the warnings back.
steps.title: Verify your domain

steps.detail: Copy the sample install URL from the Distribution tab and share it. Any account can install, no review, but installs cap at 25 until you are listed, and unlisted installs show trust warnings (see blockers).
steps.title: Distribute via the install URL

steps.detail: (To lift the 25 cap and remove warnings) First reach at least 3 active, unique, unaffiliated production installs with real activity in the past 30 days (your own and test accounts do not count). Then submit the listing: OAuth as sole auth method, scopes all used and mirrored in Shared data, live public docs/support/ToS/privacy URLs, Technology Partner Program Agreement. Manual review: initial review within 10 business days, full process no more than 60 days from first feedback (stated).
steps.time: Listing prep ~half a day; review per stated timelines
steps.title: (Optional) List on the Marketplace

tagline: Anyone can install your app the same day, no review, once you sign one policy. The catch is scale: installs cap at 25 until you pass a Marketplace listing review that itself demands 3 real customers first.

time.active: ~1 hr of app configuration + ~half a day of OAuth server code
time.total: Same day to first customer installs; listing (to scale past 25) runs on a stated 10-business-day initial review and up to 60-day full process, after you recruit 3 external installs
time.waiting: None to distribute; listing review as stated above
